newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to pay 6 trillion roubles back wages in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Russia to pay 6 trillion roubles back wages in Aug.

text.p: Russia will pay soldiers, police and scientific workers almost six trillion roubles ($1.03 billion) in August in back wages, First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov said on Monday.

Petrov told a news conference the government was supposed to settle debts of four trillion roubles ($689.8 million) to the Defence Ministry and 0.9 trillion roubles ($155.2 million) to the Internal Affairs Ministry, by the end of August.
In addition, the government would pay scientists 920 billion roubles ($158.6 million) in August, he said.
"Despite the significant amount being paid out, we will try to ease the pressure on the budget," Petrov said.

The government has vowed to press ahead, despite parliamentary opposition, with massive spending cuts under the 1997 budget after a 40 percent shortfall in tax revenues in the first three months of the year.

Petrov said the money for paying back wages was being paid out of funds raised through recent sell-offs of state property, including a quarter share in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, and a 40 percent stake in Tyumen oil company.

"The Svyazinvest sale helped us a great deal -- as a budget maker I am pleased with the results," said Petrov, adding that soldiers' back wages would be paid with the $1.330 billion the government received out of a total $1.875 billion from the sale.

Petrov said the Tyumen oil company sale gave the government 500 billion roubles ($86.2 million), with another 500 billion roubles in back taxes owed by its subsidiaries. The next tranche of a $10 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund is due in August.

He said the government securities market, which yielded 5.1 trillion roubles ($879.5 million) for state coffers in June, would also provide some income, although overall for the year it would give about five trillion roubles less than the 49 trillion ($8.4 billion) forecast.

He said the Finance Ministry was currently discussing with regional governments a plan for paying off 12 trillion roubles ($2.07 billion) in back wages still owed workers, mainly doctors and teachers.
